heroLead: Mount Pleasant sits in a part of Westmoreland County where coal, coke, and now natural gas have all left their mark on the same ground, sometimes on the same deed.
intro: This area was once part of the Connellsville coke region, and a lot of local land carries old coal reservations from that era. Whether your family's oil and gas rights were part of those old transactions or kept entirely separate is exactly the kind of question that requires real title research rather than a guess.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Mount Pleasant directly. We do that title work through the county records ourselves and explain what we find in plain terms before making an offer.

sections.heading: The Coke Region's Layered Deeds
paragraphs: The coke ovens that once lined this part of Westmoreland County required buying up coal rights across huge swaths of land, and those old transactions sometimes reserved oil and gas separately for the surface owner, sometimes didn't. That distinction still matters for anyone holding minerals near Mount Pleasant today.
Marcellus development has reached this part of the county over the past decade, with operators pooling both large farm tracts and smaller legacy parcels into horizontal units.

sections.heading: Confirming What Survived the Coal Era
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg, checking specifically for coal-era reservation language that might affect your current oil and gas interest.
If we find your family's gas rights came through the coal era intact, that's genuinely good news and we'll explain exactly why.

sections.heading: Deductions on a Historically Complicated Title
paragraphs: Older leases in this area sometimes predate current royalty protections. We'll review your specific lease's deduction language and how it compares to Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act floor before we ever discuss a number.

faqs.question: How do I know if my gas rights survived the old coal transactions?
faqs.answer: That requires checking the actual recorded deeds for reservation language specific to your parcel, which we do as part of our review at no cost to you.

faqs.question: Is Mount Pleasant still seeing active Marcellus development?
faqs.answer: Yes, operators have continued developing acreage in this part of Westmoreland County, and we evaluate your specific unit's activity as part of our review.

faqs.question: What if my family's deed is over a hundred years old?
faqs.answer: That's common in this part of the county given its coal and coke history, and we're experienced working through older deed language to confirm current ownership.
